2027-02-16.title: Tuesday of the First Week of Lent
readings: My word shall not return to me empty
From all their distress God rescues the just
Pray then in this way: Our Father in heaven
2027-02-16.alt: Lenten weekday, First Week of Lent. The Alleluia is omitted throughout Lent; the Gloria is omitted except on solemnities and feasts. Liturgical colour: violet.
2027-02-16.verse: so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.
theo: Isaiah gives us one of the most beautiful images in Scripture. “For as the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and do not return there until they have watered the earth, making it bring forth and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater, so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty.” Anyone who has watched the first monsoon rains soak a dry Kerala field knows what this means. The rain does not argue with the soil; it simply sinks in, and in time the field turns green. God's Word works in the same patient way. In Lent we are invited to let that Word fall on us daily, through the readings at Mass, the Psalms, a quiet page of the Gospel. We may not see the fruit at once. But the Word never returns empty. And the deepest meaning of this promise is Christ himself, the Word made flesh, who came down from heaven and returned to the Father only when he had accomplished all that he was sent to do.

In the Gospel Jesus teaches us how to pray. “Do not heap up empty phrases as the Gentiles do; for they think that they will be heard because of their many words… your Father knows what you need before you ask him.” Prayer is not a way of informing God or wearing him down. It is the trusting speech of children. Then he gives the Our Father: seven petitions, first for God's name, kingdom and will, then for our bread, our forgiveness and our deliverance. And Jesus adds just one comment, on only one petition: “if you do not forgive others, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.” The Word that came down from heaven teaches us the prayer that goes up to heaven, and it carries a condition: the mercy we ask for must flow on through us.
outline: Ask: have you ever watched rain soak into dry ground?
Point 1 · Rain that does not return empty
The Father knows what we need.
Point 3 · Forgive us as we forgive
“It shall not return to me empty.”
live: Read the daily Gospel slowly every day this Lent.
Pray it once today phrase by phrase, pausing at “as we also have forgiven”.
2027-02-16.prayer: Our Father in heaven, your Word comes down like rain and does not return to you empty. Let it soak into our hearts this Lent and bear fruit. Teach us to pray as your children, without empty words, and give us hearts that forgive as we have been forgiven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At every Mass, just before Communion, we pray together the prayer the Lord taught us, and then exchange a sign of peace. Forgiveness prepares us to receive the Word made flesh.

quick: God's Word is like rain: it always brings fruit.
Jesus teaches us not to babble but to trust the Father.
In the Our Father we promise to forgive as we are forgiven.
2027-02-16.action: Pray the Our Father slowly, and forgive one person by name.
2027-02-16.question: Which word of God has been falling on me without my letting it sink in?

family.explain: Jesus taught his friends to pray to God as our Father. We do not need many words, because God already knows what we need. And we promise to forgive others as God forgives us.
family.intention: We pray for families who find it hard to forgive.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone we need to forgive before we say the Our Father tonight?”

illus: A grandmother in a village near Pala prayed the Our Father with her family every night for fifty years. When her eldest son quarrelled with his brother over land and stopped coming home, she kept praying it, but she began to stop at “as we forgive those who trespass against us” and wait in silence. One evening the son, visiting for her birthday, heard the silence and asked why. She said: I am waiting for you to finish the sentence. The next week he went to see his brother.

pm.open: Father, your Word does not return to you empty. Let it fall on us like rain and bear fruit. Amen.
share: It shall not return to me empty (Isaiah 55:11). Where has God's Word borne fruit in my life?
Your Father knows what you need before you ask him (Matthew 6:8). Do I trust him?
As we also have forgiven our debtors (Matthew 6:12). Whom do I still need to forgive?
pm.resp: Our Father, forgive us as we forgive.
interc: For all who read and preach the Word of God.
For those who have stopped praying.
For families divided by quarrels over property or money.
For farmers waiting for rain and harvest.
For our group, that the Our Father may shape our lives.
pm.close: Father, your Son taught us to call you by name. Keep us faithful to his prayer and generous in forgiving. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, God says through Isaiah: as the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and do not return there until they have watered the earth… so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty (Isaiah 55:10–11).
We hear many words every day. God's Word is different: it does what it says. Let us give it room this Lent, a few minutes each day with the Gospel, and trust that it will bear fruit in its own time.
In the Gospel Jesus says: do not heap up empty phrases… your Father knows what you need before you ask him (Matthew 6:7–8). Then he teaches us the Our Father. It is the prayer of children who trust.
Jesus explains only one line of it: if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you (Matthew 6:14). Today, before we pray it, let us forgive someone by name. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus taught us a special prayer: the Our Father. Tonight, say it slowly with your family, and when you say “as we forgive those who trespass against us”, think of someone you can forgive.

intro: Theme: “It shall not return to me empty.”
The fruitful Word, the trusting prayer of children, and the forgiveness that the Our Father requires.

points.h: Rain that does not return empty
sub: Seed for the sower, bread for the eater.
q: so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.

Indeed, the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing until it divides soul from spirit, joints from marrow; it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
points.apply: Read the day's Gospel every morning of Lent.

q: Never be rash with your mouth, nor let your heart be quick to utter a word before God, for God is in heaven, and you upon earth; therefore let your words be few.
Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
points.apply: Spend five minutes of prayer today in silent trust.

q: Forgive your neighbor the wrong he has done, and then your sins will be pardoned when you pray.
For if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you;
points.apply: Forgive one person by name before you pray tonight.

concl: God's Word never falls in vain.
The prayer Jesus taught makes us children who forgive.
2027-02-16.resolve: Pray the Our Father slowly each night this week as a family.
